stats.layers.scope: {{threat}} attack runs and {{normal}} normal-work runs were counted. {{other}} runs without a ground truth (condition cells and the like) are left out of this table.
stats.mix.title: Contexa decision mix
stats.mix.caption: {{count}} resolved engine decisions
stats.method.title: How it is counted
stats.method.scope: Only completed real runs are counted. Runs with a development-only forced decision are left out, and the {{failed}} runs stopped by a technical problem are kept apart.
stats.method.decisive: Data left and blocked are counted only for scenes with a ground truth (threat or normal), from the business result of the same decisive request the comparison screen shows. A scene without a set decisive request is read at its last request.
stats.method.challenge: Normal work that met an extra check is counted apart, not as blocked. In an attack scene an extra check counts as stopped.
stats.method.unresolved: When the engine could not finish the analysis (a malformed response, a technical fault) it is not counted as a decision but as unresolved. If the data left meanwhile, it counts as data left.

adopt.title: Adopt Contexa: attach, watch, enforce
adopt.lead: Start with one dependency and a few annotations. Record decisions in Shadow mode first, then switch to enforcement once reviewed.
adopt.attach.title: Attach
adopt.attach.body: Add the starter dependency, put @EnableAISecurity on the application and @Protectable on the business methods to protect. sync = true applies the decision before the response.
adopt.observe.title: Watch
adopt.observe.body: In Shadow mode decisions are recorded but nothing is stopped. See what would have been stopped, without affecting operations.
adopt.observe.challenge: Would have asked for an extra check
adopt.observe.note: Counted from this demo’s {{count}} real engine decisions. In Shadow mode they would only have been recorded, not enforced.
adopt.enforce.title: Enforce
adopt.enforce.body: Once reviewed, switch decisions to enforcement. A value saved on the admin screen takes precedence over the setting.
adopt.legacy.title: Legacy systems
adopt.legacy.body: Connect the existing sign-in to Spring Security authentication, and the bridge passes it to Contexa as decision evidence. The existing security chain stays as it is.

exp.eyebrow: CONTEXA DEMO · two minutes, hands on
exp.title: A correct password can still carry a dangerous request
exp.body: Contexa judges every request of a signed-in user in context. Press the button yourself to send the same request to five security approaches for real, and compare what comes back.
exp.steps.label: Steps
exp.steps.2: Send it as the real owner
exp.attack.label: Scene 1 · The attacker
exp.attack.title: You have stolen administrator A's password
exp.attack.body: The sign-in worked and the administrator role is intact. Try to pull the company's core design documents out in one go.
exp.attack.expect: The right answer: this is an attack, so stop it
exp.attack.held: Contexa asked for an identity check. The code goes to administrator A's mailbox, which you as the attacker do not have, so you cannot go further.
exp.attack.giveUp: Give up and see the result
exp.attack.next: Scene 2: what if it is the real owner?
exp.owner.label: Scene 2 · The real owner
exp.owner.title: This time it is the real administrator A
exp.owner.body: A GB-500 system failure hit at dawn and the recovery needs the design documents. An incident ticket is open. Press the same button.
exp.owner.expect: The right answer: this is legitimate work, so let it pass
exp.compare.title: Same request, two situations: who got both right?
exp.compare.body: Both requests had the same account, role, time and document count; only the incident ticket differed.

exp.free.body: Change who sends it, when, how many documents and in what situation. Every press sends a real request and marks what changed from the previous result.
